refused.refusal: Kubernetes connections take no user name: basic authentication is refused. Clear User, and put a bearer token under Token or a client certificate under SSL / TLS. Nothing was sent.

hints.text: The API server: a host name or address, or a pasted https:// address such as https://api.example:6443, which is split into Host and Port. A path, such as Rancher's /k8s/clusters/<id>, goes under API path. If Studio runs in a container, localhost is that container: use the cluster's Docker network or host.docker.internal. A typed address also needs SSL Mode under SSL / TLS: verify-full with the cluster's CA, or verify-system; the default, disable, is refused for any host but this machine.
kubeadm, k3s and kind serve on 6443; managed clusters (EKS, GKE, AKS, Rancher) usually on 443.

A bearer token, without the word Bearer. A ServiceAccount token bound to view or studio-reader is the safest choice; kubectl create token lasts one hour unless --duration says otherwise. Leave empty when a client certificate under SSL / TLS signs in, or for kubectl proxy.
Empty means default, as kubectl reads it: the namespace the tree opens on and the console reads when a statement names none.
Optional: the namespaces the tree lists, separated by commas or spaces. Set it when this identity may not list namespaces; Studio then reads no namespace list.
Optional: a path every request goes under, such as /k8s/clusters/c-m-abc12 for a cluster behind Rancher.
Optional: the name the API server's certificate is checked against, when it differs from Host (kubeconfig tls-server-name).

format.sentence: Default namespace must be a DNS-1123 label: at most 63 lower-case letters, digits or hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit. Nothing was sent.
Namespaces must list DNS-1123 labels separated by commas or spaces: at most 63 lower-case letters, digits or hyphens each, starting and ending with a letter or digit. Nothing was sent.
